verdict: Caution — lend selectively to small owner-run F&B and budget-stay operators with verified cash flows; avoid leveraged new-build hotel capex and thin-margin standalone restaurants until wage and staffing pressure settles.
title: Amritsar Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A hotel or restaurant in Amritsar converts a fixed asset (rooms, kitchen, tables) plus a variable labour force into daily cash at the counter.** Revenue is same-day or same-week cash; the cost base is wages, food and beverage input, power, and rent or EMI. Value sits in location and footfall near the Golden Temple circuit, not in the building itself. **The working-capital cycle is short and favourable — guests pay before or at service — so the real risk is fixed cost, not receivables.** Capex is heavy and lumpy: a new property ties up capital for years before it earns. So when a proposal lands, check the debt-service cover against a normal, not a peak, season; if the promoter's own equity is thin, ask what funds the first two quiet months.

## What has changed now
**Wages have jumped: monthly salaries for servers and waitstaff have risen from Rs 11,000-Rs 12,000 six months ago to Rs 16,000-Rs 18,000 at present [1].** The supply of hotels, lodges, serais, guest houses, bed-and-breakfasts, restaurants, dhabas and bars has grown faster than the workforce [1], and poaching is frequent [1]. **That is a direct hit to the thin margin of a standalone restaurant, which cannot easily pass it on.** Against this, a Rs 400 crore Trident hotel project has been announced for Amritsar [2] — new branded supply that will compete for the same staff and guests. Peer results are strong but national, not local: ITC Hotels consolidated revenue up 26 percent and EBITDA up 37 percent in Q2 FY27 [4]; Leela's Q2 driven by 30 percent RevPAR growth, ARR-led [6]. **Read peers as proof that branded, well-capitalised operators are winning — not as evidence about a 20-room Amritsar lodge.** The data pack gives no local score [D], and sources say little about this city's occupancy or ARR, so lean on first principles and the wage fact.

## Where to grow
**Pursue owner-run dhabas and mid-market restaurants with steady local plus pilgrim footfall, and budget stays with proven occupancy.** These convert cash daily and can absorb a wage rise by trimming menu or staff mix. **Avoid leveraged greenfield hotel capex and single-outlet restaurants with no cushion** — the Trident announcement [2] and wage inflation [1] squeeze exactly these. For any new-build, insist on a branded or management-contract structure with limited promoter capital outlay, as peers use [11].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against seasonality: size the loan on the lean month, not the festival month.** Take monthly stock and cash statements, GST returns, and a staff-cost ratio; if wages cross the level the outlet can carry at current menu prices, ask for the revised price list. **Covenant a minimum monthly cash cover and a cap on new debt.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Staff attrition rising or wages renegotiated upward again [1] -> re-run cash cover and tighten limit.**
- **Falling covers or room nights for two straight months -> ask for the reason and pause fresh disbursal.**
- **Promoter injecting personal funds to meet salaries -> treat as stress, not support.**
watch: ratio rises above agreed cap -> ask for revised menu pricing or staff plan
cash cover falls below covenant -> freeze limit and review
turnover dips two months running -> site visit and re-rating
wages rise again -> re-run lean-month cover
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Acute staff shortage and wage jump squeeze thin-margin local operators.
